clue.text: Sly casino pays out, covering hospital therapy

indicators.note: covering means the scrambled letters wrap around the abbreviation for hospital
out here means put out of order, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A crafty casino pays out winnings while also funding someone's hospital treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SLY CASINO PAYS, and 'covering' wraps that around H for hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis is a form of talking treatment for the mind, so it is a kind of therapy.

clue.text: Scrapped fat oozed out

parts.note: squab can be an adjective meaning short and fat, squat
blood that oozed out of a wound bled

explanation.surface: Discarded fat seeped out, as when meat is trimmed and the grease runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapped' reads as thrown away, but it is the past tense of scrap, to fight; SQUAB is an old word for squat or plump.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is slang for to fight or quarrel, and squabbled means quarrelled noisily.

clue.text: Two-timer caught by US police

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the heat is American slang for the police

explanation.surface: An unfaithful lover is arrested by American cops.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer deceives a partner, and a person who is unfaithful in love is called a cheat.

clue.text: Criticise unnaturally great job hemming uniform

indicators.note: hemming means enclosing, as a hem goes round, so the scrambled letters surround the U
unnaturally says the words great job are put into an unnatural order

parts.note: Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a suspiciously impressive piece of work done on a uniform's hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnaturally' rearranges GREAT JOB, and 'hemming' puts U (Uniform in the radio alphabet) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Objurgate is a formal word meaning to scold or rebuke sharply, a synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Bond star rising to embrace old flame

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the former partner goes within the other letters
rising in a down clue means the word for star is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star
an old flame is a former lover, an ex

explanation.surface: A James Bond film star on the rise is hugging a former girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007, but it is a plain link or tie; 'rising' works because this is a down clue, and 'to embrace' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link between things, which is a bond.

clue.text: Burden left to current power

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
power in the sense of capability is ability

explanation.surface: A load left to be carried by the current in power, like a government's inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the symbol for electric current in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a responsibility or debt that weighs on someone, so it is a burden.

clue.text: Bail out of special cage

parts.note: a coop is a cage or pen for poultry

explanation.surface: Someone is released on bail from a special prison cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail out' suggests legal release, but here it means scooping water from a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail out a boat is to ladle water from it, which is to scoop it out.

clue.text: Became aware of spiralling descent

indicators.note: spiralling means twisting round, so the letters of descent are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone realised they were in a spinning dive, as a pilot might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiralling' rearranges DESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have scented something is to have sniffed it out, figuratively to have sensed or noticed it.

clue.text: One rearing fish perhaps in distant French sea

parts.note: far means distant
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A creature raising fish somewhere far off in the waters off France.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farmer breeds fish in pens, and anyone who rears livestock is a farmer.

clue.text: Extreme characters on river that's blue

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Something about the letters at the alphabet's ends, set beside a river that runs blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-coloured shade, so it is a blue.

clue.text: Put together project involving unknown and anonymous model

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for project encloses the unknown

parts.note: to project is to stick out, to jut
X is the classic algebraic unknown
A is an abbreviation for anonymous, as on poems
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: A design project combines an unnamed, anonymous model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts X inside JUT; 'project' is the verb meaning stick out, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To juxtapose is to place things side by side for contrast, so to put them together.

clue.text: Male crustacean with head hidden in hood

indicators.note: head hidden says the first letter of the crustacean word is concealed and dropped

parts.note: a lobster is a large crustacean

explanation.surface: A male crustacean whose head is tucked inside a hood, like a hermit crab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head hidden' drops the L from LOBSTER. 'hood' is the gangster sense, short for hoodlum, not headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is slang short for hoodlum, a gangster, so it means a mobster.

clue.text: Sticks around to canoodle a little bit

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for sticks is read backwards

parts.note: pins stick things together, so sticks gives pins
to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle, to pet

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about in order to kiss and cuddle for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks around' reads as lingering, but 'Sticks' is the noun for pins and 'around' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or scrap, just a little bit of something.

clue.text: Artefact old priest found in reinforced concrete

indicators.note: found in says the priest sits inside the other abbreviation

parts.note: RC is the standard abbreviation for reinforced concrete
Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digs up an ancient cleric entombed in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the Biblical priest who taught the boy Samuel, a crossword stalwart.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, which is an artefact.

clue.text: Small hole in dark pink material

indicators.note: in places the tiny opening within the colour word

parts.note: coral is a deep pinkish-red colour
a pore is a tiny opening in skin

explanation.surface: A tiny hole has appeared in some deep pink fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like the cloth the surface describes, but it is the adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, belonging to the material world rather than the spiritual.

clue.text: A fine French policeman regularly attends sick

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
flic is French slang for a police officer

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of attends

explanation.surface: A French cop who is fined keeps showing up for his sick colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of aTtEnDs, giving TED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be afflicted is to be troubled by illness, so it can mean sick.

clue.text: Tense after forceful last word? Heavens above!

indicators.note: after places the tense letter at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: firm can mean strong and forceful
amen is the final word said at the end of a prayer
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise from someone tense after a forceful closing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens above!' reads as an exclamation, but it is the literal sky overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, the heavens arching above the earth.

clue.text: Shelter head of contracts during buyout

indicators.note: during puts that letter inside the word for a buyout, within its span

parts.note: a buyout of a company is a takeover

indicators.note: head of takes just the first letter of contracts

explanation.surface: Executives look for shelter as the lead on contracts surfaces mid-acquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' picks C from contracts and 'during' sets it inside TAKEOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To take cover is to find protection from danger, which is to shelter.

clue.text: German and English back covering up Welsh bloomers?

parts.note: und is the German word for and

indicators.note: covering up means enclosing, so the word for back wraps the Welsh letter

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A German and an Englishman back away, hiding a Welshman's botanical blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering up' puts W inside REAR. 'bloomers' looks like mistakes or flowers; the question mark flags it as one example of knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are a kind of loose knickers, so they are an example of underwear.

clue.text: Defenceless university managed to rise above heads of mediocre Education Department

indicators.note: to rise in a down clue means the word for managed is read upwards

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it, so ran

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A university bettered a poor education department and left it powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns RAN into NAR in this down clue; 'heads of' takes M, E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without weapons cannot protect themselves, so unarmed means defenceless.

clue.text: Agreement to carry one thousand leads to alarmed expression

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the agreement word encloses the others

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one
K is short for a thousand, as in a 10K run

explanation.surface: Agreeing to haul a thousand items prompts a cry of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts I and K inside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an exclamation of shock or fear, so it is an alarmed expression.

clue.text: Fixed small meal at beginning and end of day

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
tea is a light evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: beginning and end of takes the first and last letters of day

explanation.surface: A small meal is fixed for the start and close of each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning and end of' takes D and Y from day. In Britain tea can mean an early-evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means firmly in place and not moving, which is fixed.

clue.text: Jar arm and hop around before applying a tiny bit of arnica

indicators.note: around means moved about, so the letters of arm and hop are rearranged
a tiny bit of takes only the first letter of arnica

explanation.surface: Someone who has jarred an arm hops about before dabbing on some arnica cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the anagram and 'a tiny bit of' takes one letter of arnica. 'Jar' looks like a verb about a knock, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel, a kind of jar.

clue.text: Cheek served up on gold dish

indicators.note: served up in a down clue reads the word for cheek upwards

parts.note: lip means cheek, impudent talk
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An impudent waiter serves something on a gold plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns LIP into PIL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice dish cooked in stock, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Male buried in powerful drift

indicators.note: buried in means set inside, so the male letter goes within the word for powerful

parts.note: able means capable, powerful

explanation.surface: A man caught in a strong snowdrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drift' looks like a snow heap but is the verb, to wander aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk slowly and casually, much as to drift along.

clue.text: Perhaps a piece of heart I cleaned

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Perhaps a bit of the heart was cleaned up, as in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition was 'Perhaps' alone, but 'a' belongs to it: the word a is an example of the thing defined, with 'Perhaps' flagging the example.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite article, so it is one example of this part of speech.

clue.text: Short story about nail

indicators.note: short means cut off its last letter, so the word for story loses its end

parts.note: a tale is a story
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A brief tale centred on a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims TALE to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's claw, which is a kind of nail.

clue.text: Label meal cooked in plastic

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with, as accounts are cooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A food label says the meal was cooked in a plastic container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges LABEL MEAL. 'plastic' is the adjective meaning mouldable, not the packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means easily moulded or shaped, which is malleable.

clue.text: Black and blue hat worn by 6

indicators.note: worn by means the hat is put on the number, so the numeral goes inside the hat word

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Someone is furious and bruised because their hat is being worn by another.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down, but it is just the number six as VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid describes the dark bluish colour of a bruise, so it means black and blue.

clue.text: Noted nude rebel broadcast something a little risque

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known naked rebel is shown on television, which is a little risque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges NOTED NUDE REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A double entendre is a phrase with a second, usually saucy meaning, so it is mildly risque.
